answer: Each identity binds to one island claim whose id hashes a unique work transcript. Credit accrues only as glacier layers: a non-replayable batch whose parent matches the prior tip, so a clone cannot splice copied history without failing the checksum. A layer seals only when a reef of independent attestors, each observing a distinct slice of that batch, signs the tip. Reusing one transcript across island claims fails: each island allows one live tip, and reef attestors refuse slices already committed elsewhere. A copied glacier has mass but no new reef signatures; unattested layers are slashed.
